`test-suggest.yml` has Claude review each function together with its
existing tests. It writes new `testthat` tests where they add value, fixes
or removes existing tests that no longer fit, **runs every new or changed
test**, and proposes only what passes as a [suggestion PR](suggestions.qmd).

## What it does

- **Every function is reviewed**, whether it already has tests or not:
  - in a pull request, push, scheduled or manual run, those in files
    that changed [since the last review](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-reviewed);
  - in a [full review](suggestions.qmd#full-review), all of them.
- **New tests only where they add value** — at most 10 per function, each
  with a stated reason, see [what gets proposed](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-proposed).
- **Existing tests are reviewed too**: outdated ones are updated, obsolete
  ones deleted, and ones that point to a bug in the code reported.
- **Every test is run** with your package loaded from source before it is
  proposed — in a separate R process without the Claude and GitHub
  tokens, since the tests are generated code. A generated test that fails
  is not proposed, but classified and reported.
- **No setup needed.** A package without `testthat` gets it set up in the
  same suggestion PR: `tests/testthat.R`, `testthat` in `Suggests`, and
  `Config/testthat/edition: 3` (only when the test runner is created; an
  existing suite keeps its edition).
- **Packages the new tests use are declared.** If a proposed test calls
  a package your `DESCRIPTION` doesn't list (e.g. `withr::local_tempdir()`),
  it is added to `Suggests` in the same suggestion PR, so R CMD check
  doesn't warn. Claude is asked to prefer base R, testthat and packages
  you already declare.

How Claude decides — what it is shown, the quality rules, the safeguards
for existing tests and how failures are classified — is on
[How tests are reviewed](test-suggest-review.qmd). Functions of DataSHIELD
packages that work on DataSHIELD connections run their tests against
DSLite, see [DataSHIELD packages](test-suggest-datashield.qmd).

## Test files {#test-files}

Your test files are found in either of two naming schemes:

- **`tests/testthat/test-<R file>.R`**, the usual one, e.g.
  `test-ds.mean.R` for `R/ds.mean.R`;
- **`test-<category>-<R file>.R`**, with several files per function,
  each for one purpose: e.g. `test-arg-ds.mean.R` for argument checks
  and `test-smk-ds.mean.R` for smoke tests, as in the DataSHIELD base
  packages.

Test files are named after the **R file**, not the function — the same
thing with one function per file, as the workflows assume. All of a
function's test files are run and reviewed together, and each change
stays in its own file. Names are matched exactly: tests of
`ds.meanByClass` are never taken for tests of `ds.mean`.

**Where new tests go** depends on the scheme, which is recognised
automatically. If at least half of your test files (and at least three)
are named by category, Claude picks a category for each new test from the
ones your repository uses, and the test goes into
`test-<category>-<R file>.R`; the file is created if needed. Otherwise
new tests go into `test-<R file>.R`.

What the common categories mean (`arg`, `smk`, `disc`, `math`, …) is
explained to Claude in `config/test-categories.yml`; a category without
an entry is shown with your existing files of that category as examples.
You can add or change meanings
([per repository](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance)).

New tests are added before a file's clean-up at the end, such as a
`test_that("shutdown", …)` block or a disconnect, so they can use what the
file sets up at its start. A new file follows how your other test files
are built, e.g. connecting at the top and disconnecting at the end.

## The report

The link comment on your PR and the suggestion PR's description start with
a one-line summary, e.g. "7 new tests · 1 existing test updated · added
to Suggests: `withr` · 1 possible bug". The description is
[one report](suggestions.qmd#one-suggestion-pr-per-branch), rebuilt on
every run, with collapsible sections per test file:

- **New tests** and **changes to existing tests**, each with its reason
  and a [checkbox](suggestion-choices.qmd) — every one passed a real run;
- **Possible bugs in the code**: tests that fail because the code rather
  than the test looks wrong, with how sure Claude is and a link to their
  issue, see [failing tests](test-suggest-review.qmd#failing-tests);
- **Existing tests to look at**: reported tests and failing tests left
  unchanged;
- **Generated tests that failed**, where they aren't commented on a PR;
- for DataSHIELD packages with `dslite-setup: never`, **functions not
  tested** because the tests have no way to connect.

A test that failed in an earlier run isn't classified, commented or filed
again; a reported test that passes now is marked as resolved.

Heading sizes and spacing can be adjusted in `config/report-style.yml`
([per repository](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance)). Without a
suggestion PR, the report is posted as a comment on your PR, or, without
a PR, as an issue ([where reports go](suggestions.qmd#where-reports-go)).

## Scheduled runs and full reviews

A scheduled or manual run reviews the functions whose R file changed on
the branch since its last review, plus files whose Claude call failed
then. To review every function, start a
[full review](suggestions.qmd#full-review) (`review-scope: all`), e.g.
once when you add the workflow. A full review of a large package costs a
Claude call per function, with the stronger model the test review uses.
